title: India's Electronics Exports Hit Rs 4.24 Lakh Crore as Smartphones Become Top Export Commodity
excerpt: Electronics production surged to Rs 13.11 lakh crore in FY2025-26, up 15.8% year-on-year, with smartphones overtaking petroleum and gems as India's leading individual export item.
body:
• India's electronics exports reached Rs 4.24 lakh crore ($47.96 billion) in FY2025-26, an 11-fold increase over the past 12 years.
  • Electronics production grew 15.8% year-on-year to Rs 13.11 lakh crore, with smartphones surpassing petroleum and gems as India's top individual export commodity.
  • Mobile phone production rose 33-fold over the past decade to Rs 6.27 lakh crore, with exports surging 165-fold to Rs 2.60 lakh crore.
  • Apple iPhone exports from India hit Rs 2.03 lakh crore in 2025, nearly doubling the previous year, as companies diversify manufacturing away from China.

From Net Importer to Export Powerhouse

India's electronics manufacturing sector has completed a structural transformation that few predicted a decade ago. Electronics exports climbed to Rs 4.24 lakh crore ($47.96 billion) in FY2025-26, an 11-fold jump from Rs 38,263 crore in FY2014-15, according to data presented by Union Minister of State for Electronics and IT Jitin Prasada in the Lok Sabha.

Total electronics production rose 15.8% year-on-year to Rs 13.11 lakh crore, up from Rs 11.32 lakh crore in FY2024-25. The sector now supports an estimated 2.5 million direct and indirect jobs, with the mobile manufacturing ecosystem alone employing 1.2 million people across the value chain.

The most striking shift: smartphones, which did not feature in India's top 100 exported commodities in 2014, have now become the country's single largest individual export item, surpassing petroleum, gems, and jewelry in FY2025-26.

Apple Drives the Export Surge

Apple has emerged as the primary engine behind India's electronics export growth. iPhone exports from India reached Rs 2.03 lakh crore in calendar year 2025, nearly double the Rs 1.1 lakh crore shipped in 2024, according to government data shared by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.

The acceleration reflects Apple's deliberate strategy to diversify manufacturing away from China following US tariffs. India now produces roughly 30 crore (300 million) mobile phone units annually, with one in four smartphones manufactured in the country destined for export, according to Neil Shah, co-founder of market research firm Counterpoint.

"Apple has become a poster child for India by expanding its manufacturing post-US tariffs on China, with exports from India reaching record highs."

— Neil Shah, Co-Founder, Counterpoint Research

Mobile phone production overall expanded 33-fold over the past decade, from Rs 18,900 crore in FY2014-15 to Rs 6.27 lakh crore in FY2025-26. Exports from the mobile segment surged 165-fold, from Rs 1,566 crore to Rs 2.60 lakh crore in the same period.

Policy Framework Fueling Growth

The Production-Linked Incentive scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (PLI-LSEM) has been the primary policy catalyst. As of March 2026, the scheme attracted cumulative investments exceeding Rs 20,600 crore, while cumulative production crossed Rs 11.62 lakh crore and exports surpassed Rs 6.53 lakh crore.

The government has also launched PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT hardware to reduce import dependency on laptops, tablets, and servers. Additionally, the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme has approved 75 applications across 23 product categories, expected to attract Rs 61,671 crore in investment and generate 65,040 direct jobs.

India has reached a point where 99.2% of mobile phones used domestically are manufactured in the country, completing a transition from net importer in 2014 to net exporter. The country is now the world's second-largest mobile phone manufacturer by volume.

Semiconductor Production Adds Momentum

The electronics export trajectory is set to steepen further as India's semiconductor facilities come online. Four chip plants are expected to begin commercial production in 2026, including Micron Technology's assembly and test facility in Sanand, Gujarat, which has already shipped its first made-in-India memory modules.

"Electronics exports crossed Rs 4 lakh crore in 2025, creating jobs and bringing foreign exchange. Momentum will continue in 2026 as four semiconductor plants come into commercial production," Vaishnaw said.

The India Cellular and Electronics Association projects mobile phone production will reach $75 billion (Rs 6.76 lakh crore) in the current fiscal year, with exports accounting for over $30 billion. Electronic goods now rank as India's third-largest export category overall, behind only services and refined petroleum products — a position that seemed improbable just a decade ago.
nri_angle: India's rapid rise as an electronics manufacturing hub creates investment opportunities and signals the country's growing role in global technology supply chains.
